name: A New Century · party policy preferences
description: Govern for five years: keep household needs met, services funded and government stable. Country play continues after political transitions. Relative food/energy prices are authored rules-3 model assumptions, not sourced historical prices. The original fixed-price pack is retained for classic saves. Borrowing authority, consent delays and emergency political costs are authored rules-4 assumptions, not a reproduction of historical debt law. Earlier market and classic packs remain available for their original campaigns. Constitutional transitions use authored rules-5 templates, backing thresholds, costs and inertia rather than sourced historical amendment law. Starter AI prefers its opening governing form; fictional fixtures demonstrate alternative preferences. Earlier campaigns retain their original packs. Policy amendments, withdrawal, history and observed reviews use authored rules-6 procedures. Existing campaigns retain their exact original rules. Ministerial portfolios, generated nominees and preparation rules are authored gameplay definitions, not historical ministry rosters or vacancy claims. Unassigned portfolios use permanent civil service. Earlier campaigns retain their exact original rules. Independent electoral mandates, early-poll powers and calendar terms are authored gameplay assumptions, not historical national election law. Earlier campaigns retain their exact original rules. Population observations cover all 15 starter countries and GDP covers 14, from the pinned World Bank mirrors. North Korean GDP retains its explicit authored calibration. Annual observations are bookmark proxies; primary sources have not been independently reconciled. National/local budget charters and territorial procedures are authored gameplay abstractions. The two disjoint budget jurisdictions per country are population partitions, not historical administrative units, mapped boundaries or regional electorates. Local purchase levels, collected-tax shares, autonomy templates, compensation and consent proxies are original model assumptions. Public delivery pledges, governing support arrangements and linked project deadlines use authored procedures and credibility records, not historical campaign promises or party agreements. They do not supply resources or form cabinet coalitions. Existing policy authority and implementation constraints apply. Reviewed annual and supplementary fiscal packages use authored preparation, administration, implementation reservation and calendar accounting procedures. Enactment funds actual policy programmes; recurring purchasing remains subject to cash and delivery constraints. These plans are not historical budget laws or hard appropriation ceilings. Progressive private-income withholding uses authored representative-cohort bands relative to opening GDP per resident, not historical filing law or within-cohort distributions. Public/local service payments and welfare remain outside this base. Potential tax is not treasury cash or arrears. Nonplayer fiscal reviews use the national daily balance after protected local tax claims. A consolidated surplus cannot finance national obligations from protected local cash. Budget authority, submission funding, review and actual programme delivery remain ordinary shared constraints. This is an authored bounded heuristic, not historical government behavior or optimal economic planning. New loan principal matures an authored 365 days after actual disbursement. Opening debt remains perpetual calibration; historical debt curves and actual refinancing markets are not claimed. Temporary cash retention can protect actual national funds for a future decision, up to 1% opening GDP for 90 days, with approval cost and reuse cooldown. Unfunded targets are not cash. Release, expiry or a successor government ends protection without cancelling obligations or granting spending authority. Debt interest accrues at fixed 4% actual/365 on actual outstanding principal after scheduled redemption. Fractions carry without compounding until a whole reporting unit becomes due; only paid amounts transfer cash. Unpaid whole interest remains external arrears, while the unsettled sub-unit creditor claim survives principal retirement without becoming cash or spending authority. Tax, wage, purchase and price rounding remain whole reporting units. Existing grid and agriculture programmes have explicitly authored technology eligibility for every seeded country from the 2000 bookmark. Eligibility grants no research, adoption, cash, capacity or faster construction; ordinary authority, funding and delivery remain necessary. These dates are scenario permissions, not historical discovery or adoption records. Independently authored party fiscal ranges add delayed political tradeoffs for operating income-tax, service and welfare policies. Legislative coalitions use live seat weights; party leadership uses its ruling party. Unknown positions remain explicit, and other governing routes retain independent backing. No positions are inferred from ideology labels or claimed as sourced historical platforms. Preferences grant no resources, consent exemptions or free support. Social, institutional, regional and foreign-policy positions and dated platform evolution remain unfinished. Reference sovereignty geography remains unknown.

sources.description: Historical identity seed; see data/README.md for dated coverage and review limitations.
Original game calibration. Values, profiles and coefficients are authored except for the six explicitly recorded population/GDP observations.

World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, 2000 observation via datasets/population, revision d4b1a4a9a17e2123baf0ef119de05bceced1ab1b. Primary API not independently rechecked. See data/starter-observations.json for provenance.

World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, 2000 observation via datasets/gdp, revision 36d761dc5617982d3e50b213e02b9a1b47c4e958. Primary API not independently rechecked. See data/starter-observations.json for provenance.
Original relative-price, import, storage and basket-share assumptions. No historical price-series calibration is claimed.
Original regime-route borrowing consent, fixed-rate debt and contested emergency assumptions. No historical constitutional or debt-market calibration is claimed.

Original lawful and contested constitutional-transition templates, political costs, consent constraints and status-quo AI preferences. These are game assumptions, not historical constitutional procedures.
Original amendment administration costs, per-proposal limits and observed-review intervals. These are game assumptions, not historical legislative or contracting rules.
Original functional portfolios, generated candidate profiles, eligibility, appointment/dismissal costs and preparation delays. No historical ministerial staffing or career claims.

Original independent electoral mandates, early-poll jurisdiction, review/campaign intervals, administration costs and calendar terms. No historical poll records, national electoral law or integrity certification is claimed.

Original two-jurisdiction budget partitions, local purchasing levels, autonomy/tax-share templates, grant consent, lawful compensation and contested territorial/requisition costs. No historical territorial law, administrative geography, regional voting or local fiscal calibration is claimed.

Original public delivery pledges, conditional governing-support arrangements, linked programme deadlines, political effects, administration costs, fixed review/interval rules and record-based credibility. No historical election promises, party agreements, commercial contracts or treaties are claimed.

Original annual/supplementary fiscal preparation, institutional review, administration costs, implementation reservations and calendar execution. No historical budget law, tax-base calibration or hard appropriation ceiling is claimed.

Original representative-cohort private-income bands, GDP-per-resident thresholds, marginal rate factors and fixed 365-day annualisation. No historical tax filing law, individual distributions or national tax-base calibration is claimed.

Original national-funding review objective for the bounded fiscal AI. It respects protected local claims and shared legal/cash/implementation rules; it does not claim historical government decisions, privileged revenue or optimal planning.

Original 365-day maturity and scheduled-principal settlement for new loans. Existing authority and emergency constraints are retained; this is not historical debt calibration or default/restructuring.

Original temporary retention of actual national cash after protected local and capital claims. Deferred operating payments remain arrears; unpaid principal remains debt. Uniform authored gameplay procedure, not historical cash-management law or payment priority.

Original fixed 4% actual/365 principal-day accrual with carried fractional reporting units. Whole interest due, actual cash payments and unpaid whole-unit arrears reconcile separately. This is uniform gameplay accounting, not historical debt pricing, compounding, currency precision or legal settlement law.

Original baseline programme eligibility for the 2000 bookmark. All seeded countries may commission the existing grid and agriculture programmes from the bookmark, subject to ordinary funding and governing authority. Dates denote scenario permissions, not historical scientific discovery, knowledge adoption or research completion.

Original party-specific fiscal ranges, relative importance and bounded monthly backing pressure for gameplay. These are not sourced historical platforms or positions inferred from ideology labels. Unknown positions remain explicit; royal, religious, personalist and military routes retain independent backing. Other preference dimensions and dated platform changes remain unknown.

policies.name: Standard private-income marginal rate
policies.description: Set the standard marginal reference rate for authored private-income bands. Withholding uses actual private income, representative cohort means and collection capacity; benefits and public/local wages remain outside this base. Full tax filing law and other bases are not modeled.

policies.name: Public service budget
policies.description: Annual spending as % of modeled GDP. Delivery improves gradually and is limited by administrative capacity.

policies.name: Household safety net
policies.description: Annual transfers as % of modeled GDP. Payments reach household accounts only when funded.

policies.name: Energy capacity program
policies.description: Build 15 percentage points of domestic energy coverage. Capital is reserved during consent and paid before implementation; operating costs begin on completion.

policies.name: Food resilience program
policies.description: Build 15 percentage points of food supply. Requires time and funded maintenance.

policies.name: Civil service modernization
policies.description: Increase administrative capacity by 8 points, improving tax collection and service delivery.

policies.name: Negotiate governing support
policies.description: Negotiate with parliamentary partners; adds up to 12 support points for the present government. Bargaining uses administrative resources.
